shim.script:
#!/bin/sh
# Recording shim: no docker daemon exists in this disposable container.
# Every INVOCATION appends one record starting with `ts=`; an argv that itself
# contains newlines (a `sh -c` script) continues on the following lines, so the
# invocation count is `grep -c '^ts='` and NOT `wc -l`.
# The shim itself is mounted read-only at /shim; its log lands on a writable
# mount of the same host directory at /shimlog/.
{
  printf 'ts=%s pid=%s cwd=%s argv=' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$$" "$PWD"
  printf '%s ' "$@"
  printf '\n'
} >> /shimlog/docker-calls.log 2>&1
echo "docker shim: no docker daemon in this disposable container (call recorded)" >&2
exit 127
shim.mounting: the shim is mounted read-only at /shim and its log lands in the same host directory mounted writable at /shimlog, so the record survives with the shim itself immutable; the log is retained as <run>/shim/docker-calls.log

recorded_intent_not_execution.what: a shim-refused `docker create` is recorded intent: the log line carries the timestamp, pid, cwd and argv only, and the refusal status 127 appears in no log line. The status comes from the retained shim script itself (each run keeps its own copy beside its log, at delivered/<run>/shim/docker): the shim appends the record, writes its "no docker daemon" note to stderr, and then `exit 127` unconditionally, without appending the status to the log.
